content:
Phase 36 implemented on branch phase-36-visual-story (findings: docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-findings.md; every in-cycle gate recorded there). Docs, media, scripts and tests only — `git diff origin/main -- tagteam/` is 0 lines and the built 3.0.0 wheel's 86 tagteam/ entries have the same file list and sha256 hashes as the 0.12.0 wheel from PyPI.

Delivered: (A) README restructured in the reader's order around four mermaid blocks (① loop flowchart, ② one-cycle stateDiagram with "REQUEST_CHANGES after 10 consecutive stale rounds (auto)", ③ Manual → Watched → Headless → + Cockpit & Hub ladder, ④ headless architecture), cockpit + hub screenshots, reference tail kept, license/link-back paragraph kept; (B) docs/how-tagteam-works.md — every deep paragraph moved verbatim under stable anchors (#loop #cycle #modes #headless #controls #escalations #cockpit #hub #saloon #files) + "Files tagteam writes" table; (C) docs/media/: tagteam-loop/cycle/modes/headless.svg in the Aegis conventions (viewBox 800×260/260/240/260, role=img + aria-label, no external refs, 3–6 KB, node labels class="node" matched to the README mermaid by test), three 1280×800 PNG screenshots from SEEDED projects (scripts/showcase_seed.py: demo-api escalated + brief → Needs you; demo-web owed/stale → Waiting; demo-docs approved → Quiet; hub started with --registry on the seed file), manifest with slots/alt/conventions/recipe/public-safety checklist; (D) docs/showcase.md with the marked numbers block (as-of 2026-08-15 UTC — chosen so this impl cycle's own 08-16 entries cannot stale it; rationale in findings) and a real abridged Phase 35 plan cycle quoted from the tracked JSONL; (E) scripts/showcase_numbers.py `report --as-of [--usage] [--json]` + `export-usage --as-of` (inclusive UTC day, filter-before-strip, per-(phase,type,round,role) attempt ordinal, 13-key schema, sort_keys, exit 2 on mismatch/missing as-of; stale streak = copy of cycle._count_stale_rounds' loop); (F) scripts/upgrade_smoke.py — `<--python> -I -c` helper with cwd in a temp dir outside the repo, identity line (executable/prefix/version/resolved file) + `go` handshake, parent verifies interpreter identity and (with --expect-version) version + file-under-prefix before go, temp registry = exactly one entry, fail-closed registry-global assertion in the helper, existence+sha256 snapshots of the real registry / every real project's managed destinations / project / sentinel, exit 0 no-op / 1 project changed / 2 isolation or identity failure; (G) tests: tests/test_docs_story.py (20: fences/links/anchors, mermaid lint, SVG conventions incl. only the xmlns URL allowed, SVG↔mermaid labels, PNG IHDR/no-text-chunks, CLI coverage, glossary guard, 5-second test), tests/test_showcase_numbers.py (7: fixture methodology incl. ruling/AMEND/in-progress/legacy dedupe/as-of boundary, production stale rule 11→10, export contract with shuffled duplicate attempts + boundary + byte-stability, mismatched as_of → exit 2, committed snapshot safety, byte-compare of the showcase block), tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py (5: isolated no-op with sentinel + real registry byte-identical, project-changed still isolated, real temp venv with a same-named stub package launched from the checkout cwd → not shadowed, wrong version refused before go, default interpreter reports the checkout). Full suite 931 passed / 5 skipped. Bookkeeping: pyproject + CITATION.cff → 3.0.0, roadmap, proposal §5 note.

Gates: mermaid rendered with mermaid@11 in Chrome (4/4, no syntax errors; docs/phases/media/phase-36-mermaid-render-{1,2}.jpg); SVGs dropped into a local copy of aegis.html's flow/tiers/vis slots (phase-36-portfolio-dropin.jpg); screenshot public-safety checklist item by item (token meta-only — 64-char value absent from visible text; no absolute path in visible text; only the 3 seed entries; all round text authored in the seed; PNG chunks); upgrade smoke through the harness only: 0.12.0 wheel in a scratch venv, 0.12.0 setup run in a fresh -I process with patched registry globals + fail-closed assertion, source harness → no-op, sentinel untouched, temp registry one entry, real registry byte-identical (cmp), exit 0; installed-wheel-mode dry run `--python <0.12.0 venv> --expect-version 0.12.0` → identity = the venv's site-packages tagteam, no-op; `--expect-version 3.0.0` → exit 2 before go. Evidence the -I/external-cwd rule matters: the same venv without -I from the checkout cwd imported the checkout's tagteam.

Deviations for you (findings "Deviations"): README 238 lines excl. mermaid vs ≤200 target (reference tail kept verbatim); the shipped cockpit Usage chart's own "r10 auto-escalate" wording (Phase 34 cockpit.js) is left untouched to honor the zero-package-diff contract — proposed 3.0.1 follow-up; harness tests in tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py (not test_docs_story.py) and the stub venv gets the package copied into purelib (--without-pip, no network) instead of pip-installing a built sdist; seed stores the brief path project-relative because the Feed prints it.

The implementation is polished and the verification is strong: the focused tests pass, the complete suite passes (931 passed, 5 skipped), `git diff --check` is clean, the upgrade harness is fail-closed and isolated, and the rendered screenshots/SVGs are readable. Three correctness issues block approval:

1. Fix canonical-cycle precedence before the as-of filter in `scripts/showcase_numbers.py::load_cycles`. The documented contract says `docs/handoffs/` wins over `.tagteam/legacy/`, but the current code records a key in `seen` only after at least one canonical entry survives the cutoff. If the canonical cycle has only post-cutoff entries, an older legacy cycle with the same `(phase, type)` is accepted and resurrects superseded history. Reproduction: canonical `docs/handoffs/dup_plan` entry dated 2026-05-09, legacy duplicate approved on 2026-05-01, cutoff 2026-05-08; `load_cycles` currently returns the legacy approval, while the cycle should be excluded. Reserve/select the canonical key before filtering, and add this exact regression case.

2. Do not ship a public 3.0 visual that knowingly states the false rule. `docs/media/screenshots/cockpit-usage.png` prominently says “the round-10 line is auto-escalation” / “r10 auto-escalate”, from `tagteam/data/web/cockpit.html:87` and `tagteam/data/web/cockpit.js:543`, while the README correctly says escalation occurs after 10 consecutive unchanged re-submissions and progressing cycles can exceed round 10. Correct the cockpit wording (for example, a stale-round-limit label), recapture the seeded screenshot, and add coverage that prevents the old round-number wording from returning. This is a correctness-driven exception to the planned zero-package-diff target: update the findings/release comparison to disclose and narrowly verify the text-only package change. If package immutability is retained instead, the known-false usage screenshot cannot remain a shipped portfolio asset.

3. Correct the first-screen loop diagram’s arbiter routing. README lines 22–23 and `tagteam-loop.svg` currently send a generic “ruling” from the Arbiter back to Lead plan/implementation, and both showcase/media alt texts say the ruling goes back to Lead. In reality, `request-changes` returns to the appropriate lead step, but approval closes the current cycle: plan approval advances to implementation and implementation approval advances to the next roadmap phase. Split those outcomes in the README Mermaid and standalone SVG, update both alt texts, refresh the render evidence, and extend the semantic tests so the hero diagram cannot regress while merely matching node labels.

The README length deviation is acceptable given the preserved reference tail, and the test-file/stub-install/relative-brief-path deviations do not block approval.

Round 2 — the three blockers (findings "Round 2" + updated deviations/gates; commit c99b2ee): 1. Canonical precedence before the as-of filter: `load_cycles` reserves the (phase,type) key for the first CYCLE_DIRS entry that has a status file BEFORE filtering; a canonical cycle with only post-cutoff entries is excluded and the legacy duplicate never resurfaces. Your exact reproduction is now a fixture case (canonical dup/plan dated 2026-05-09 in docs/handoffs, legacy duplicate approved 2026-05-01, as-of 2026-05-08 → ("dup","plan") absent; asserted alongside "future"). This repo has no cross-dir duplicates, so the committed numbers block is unchanged and the byte-compare stays green. 2. Cockpit wording corrected as a disclosed, text-only package change: tagteam/data/web/cockpit.html caption → "dashed line: the stale-round limit (auto-escalation after 10 consecutive stale rounds; a progressing cycle can go past it)"; cockpit.js marker label → "10-stale-round limit" (+ comment). Guard added to test_glossary_guard: both files must not contain "round-10 line" / "r10 auto-escalate" / round-10 / "10 rounds", and cockpit.html must contain "10 consecutive stale rounds". cockpit-usage.png recaptured from the seed (caption + marker visible; token absent from visible text, no absolute path). Verified narrowly: `git diff origin/main -- tagteam/` = exactly those two files (6+/4−); the rebuilt 3.0.0 wheel vs the 0.12.0 wheel from PyPI: same 86-entry file list, hashes equal for 84, differing entries exactly cockpit.html + cockpit.js; tagteam/data/web is not among the files setup/upgrade copy, so the upgrade no-op is unaffected. Plan success criterion 6 and the "Out" list amended to record the exception at your request; findings updated. Full suite 932 passed / 5 skipped. 3. Loop diagram ruling routing split: README mermaid ① now `A -. "request changes (plan)" .-> P`, `A -. "approve (plan) /
request changes (impl)" .-> I`, `A -. "approve (impl)" .-> R` (no generic "ruling"); README role bullet states the ruling takes the reviewer's seat (request changes → back to the Lead; approve closes the cycle — plan → implementation, impl → next phase); tagteam-loop.svg redrawn with the same three ruling edges (labels marked class="edge") + both escalations, aria-label updated; manifest and showcase alt texts updated. New semantic test test_loop_diagram_routes_the_arbiters_ruling_correctly parses the mermaid edges (PR→A/IR→A escalate; A→P request-changes-only with "(plan)"; A→I approve + request changes; A→R approve-only ending "(impl)"; no A→* edge labelled "ruling") and the SVG edge labels (two "escalate", the three outcomes) — and every class="edge" label must appear in the mermaid text (drift). Re-rendered with mermaid@11 (no syntax errors) alongside the SVG: docs/phases/media/phase-36-loop-render-r2.jpg.

Round 2 correctly fixes canonical source precedence and the loop/alt-text routing, with useful regression coverage. The focused suite passes (33), the complete suite passes (932 passed, 5 skipped), `git diff --check` is clean, the package diff is narrowly limited to the two disclosed cockpit files, and the refreshed loop render is semantically correct.

One public-visual correctness issue remains. The Usage chart’s x-axis is absolute cycle round (`r1 … r10`), and `cockpit.js` still draws the dashed threshold at `X(10)`. Relabelling that fixed x-coordinate “10-stale-round limit” does not make the encoding valid: ten consecutive stale re-submissions can be reached after any baseline round (for example, stale rounds 21–30), while a progressing cycle may cross r10 without any stale streak. The recaptured screenshot therefore still visually places a stale-count threshold at absolute round 10; the caption’s caveat cannot reconcile those different units. The new JS comment even notes that the marker “only gives the curve a scale,” while the UI calls it the auto-escalation limit.

Remove the fixed vertical threshold from this round-number chart and keep the accurate rule as ordinary explanatory text/legend copy that is not anchored to an x-axis round. (Alternatively, only draw a threshold if it is computed from a real stale-streak baseline and label that actual coordinate, but removal is the simpler truthful design.) Recapture `cockpit-usage.png`, update the findings, and strengthen the regression so it rejects a stale/auto-escalation marker drawn at `X(10)` rather than merely banning the old phrases. The two other requested changes are accepted and need no further revision.
